findings.title: Existing FGAPv2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type or scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore keep only the Users resource and the old scope set: the Clients all-resource resource and the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes are never created for them. Client permissions cannot be created or evaluated correctly in such upgraded realms until the admin-permissions client is recreated.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the Clients type resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code loads the Clients type resource and immediately passes it to findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null, for example in a realm created before the Clients type existed or if the type resource was not provisioned, so this dereference/query with a null resource can throw instead of simply denying the permission.

findings.title: Resource display names are not resolved for the Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() translates Users resources to 'All users' or the user's username, but has no equivalent Clients branch. Client resources therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for resources created by getOrCreateResource is based on the internal client UUID and for the type resource is the raw type name, so permission/resource listings for clients show opaque identifiers instead of 'All clients' or the clientId.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-clients pseudo-resource as a client id
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also returns the type resource whose name is literally 'Clients', created at schema initialization. If the caller is granted the scope on all clients, hasGrantedPermission succeeds for that resource and granted.add(resource.getName()) inserts 'Clients' into a set whose contract (Set<String> getClientsWithPermission) is client identifiers, while no actual client ids are added for clients that have no per-client resource yet. Callers filtering clients by id will miss those clients and may treat 'Clients' as an id.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks lose the traditional manage-clients admin fallback
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles (line 97), and canMapClientScopeRoles (line 102) return only hasPermission(client, <fgap-scope>). Unlike canManage(ClientModel), canConfigure, canManageClientScopes, and canView(ClientScopeModel) in the same class, they never check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) (directly or via canManage(client)). A realm admin holding the normal manage-clients role can manage and configure a client under FGAPv2 but is denied mapping that client's roles, composite roles, and client-scope roles unless a separate FGAP permission is also created.

findings.title: Removal listener still runs V2-unsupported operations when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The listener is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1). AdminPermissions.management() prefers MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the v2 feature is enabled, so with both v1 and v2 features enabled a ClientRemovedEvent still reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, instead of the event being skipped. The guard needs to exclude the case where v2 takes precedence (v1 enabled and v2 not enabled).
